cards.explanation: The answer is to appeal to him as to a father. Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, tells Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2), to "…appeal to him as to a father." I think a hard word lands softer when it's handed over with honor. The correction is still on the table, friends, it just comes in gently.

The answers are brothers and mothers. Paul says, "Treat younger men as brothers…" After the father for the older man, the family picture keeps going. Then he says, "…older women as mothers…" Paul is building a whole household for Timothy in a few short lines.

The answer is False. Paul says a widow's children or grandchildren "…must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents…" The family goes first, friends. Paul adds that this is pleasing in the sight of God.

The answer is that it is pleasing to Him. Paul says repaying their parents "…is pleasing in the sight of God." He doesn't say it's a chore or just a duty. God is pleased when a family takes care of its own.

The answer is in God. The widow who is truly in need and left all alone "…puts her hope in God…" And Paul says she continues night and day in her petitions and prayers. Her hope sits with God, friends, and her days are full of prayer.

The answer is that she is dead even while alive. Paul says, "…she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive." That's a strong picture, and he puts it right next to the widow who prays night and day. One lives for pleasure and the other puts her hope in God.

The word is denied. Paul says, "If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith…" He's saying providing for your family is part of living out what you believe. It's serious, friends, and Paul says it plainly.

The answer is True, and those are Paul's own words. Anyone who does not provide for his own, especially his own household, "…has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever." It's a hard thing to hear. I think Paul says it that strongly because caring for family matters so much.

The answer is at least sixty. Paul says, "A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old…" Age is just the first thing on the list, friends. She also needs to be faithful to her husband and well known for good deeds.
The word is deeds. Paul says she should be "…well known for good deeds…" Then he lists them, like bringing up children and entertaining strangers. What she's done is what people know her for.

The reason is that their passions draw them from Christ. Paul says, "For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry…" He says that leads to judgment, because they are setting aside their first faith. Paul keeps his eye on their faith, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says the younger widows will learn to be idle, "…going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention." Every good work is how he describes the widows on the list. For these younger ones he warns about idle days.

The answer is to marry and manage a household. Paul says, "So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households…" He says that denies the adversary occasion for slander. Paul gives them a clear path, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says, "For some have already turned aside to follow Satan." That's a heavy line, and we can let it be heavy. It comes right after he advises the younger widows to marry, have children and manage their households.

The answer is False. Paul says, "If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened…" She takes care of them herself, friends. Then the church can help the widows who are truly in need.
